problem_signature: YM-S1a2|same-theory OS/SZZ transfer bridge|witness-iv source density after OS null quotient|fixed-cutoff infinite-volume strong coupling
object_context: Conditional local closure of the source-family density coordinate in the fixed-cutoff strong-coupling spectral bridge. Work in one infinite-volume lattice gauge measure mu which is both gauge invariant and reflection positive for a fixed Euclidean time reflection. Determine whether centered smooth gauge-invariant positive-time cylinder sources are dense in the OS excited-state Hilbert space after the null quotient. This does not identify the SZZ measure with the physical reflection-positive measure, does not prove covariance=transfer moments, and does not address a->0/RG/continuum transport.
structural_coordinates: Q_+=G^{E_+} with compact Lie G and countable positive-time edge set E_+; positive-time cylinder functions depend on finitely many edge variables.
A_+ is the smooth gauge-invariant positive-time cylinder algebra; the OS Hilbert space is the completion of A_+/N for the reflection-positive sesquilinear form.
The same probability measure mu must supply both the L2 topology used for density and the OS reflection form; cross-measure density transfer is forbidden.
Gauge averaging is over the finite product of compact gauge groups at vertices incident to the finite source support; it preserves finite support and smoothness.
The OS seminorm must be L2-continuous: ||[F]||_OS^2=mu(conj(theta F)F)<=||theta F||_2||F||_2=||F||_2^2 when mu is reflection invariant.
Centering by mu(F) preserves cylinder smoothness and gauge invariance and lands orthogonal to Omega=[1].
Dense span, not cyclicity, is the exact hypothesis needed by YM-S1a1_C001_V2 for global spectral support exclusion.

SZZ Corollary 1.6 controls all smooth cylinder functions with one source-independent exponential distance exponent in a fixed strong-coupling infinite-volume theory, but calls this Euclidean covariance decay a mass gap; physical transfer identification remains separate.
Fixed lattice-scale volume uniformity is not lattice-spacing/continuum uniformity.
equivalent_formulations: Show q(A_+^0) is dense in Omega^perp, where A_+^0={F in A_+: mu(F)=0} and q is the OS quotient map.
Show every OS vector orthogonal to the vacuum is an OS-norm limit of centered smooth gauge-invariant positive-time cylinder source vectors.
solved_analogues: Continuous cylinder functions are uniformly dense in C(G^{E_+}) for compact metrizable product configuration spaces.
Smooth functions are dense in continuous functions on each finite compact Lie-group product G^n.
Compact-group averaging is an L2 contraction and projection onto the invariant subspace when the measure is invariant.
near_solved_analogues: YM-S1a1 dense-source spectral exclusion candidate: density plus a common transfer-moment rate would exclude hidden slow states.
SZZ smooth-cylinder covariance class is broad enough that regularity need not force a small finite source family.

method_transfers.source_context: Functional analysis on compact product spaces
method_transfers.method: Build L2 density by continuous cylinders -> smooth finite-coordinate cylinders, project to gauge invariants, then use an explicit OS-seminorm <= L2-norm inequality to transfer density through the null quotient.
required_assumptions: same mu in L2 and OS form
disanalogies: ordinary L2 density does not by itself imply density in an unrelated quotient norm
kinematic density does not identify the transfer matrix
method_transfers.repair_question: Can current source literature bind SZZ mu to the same reflection-positive OS measure and transfer operator so this local density lemma can actually glue?

explicit_disanalogies: The local density lemma is conditional and does not prove SZZ's infinite-volume measure inherits the reflection-positive OS reconstruction required here.
No equality between SZZ covariance and a physical transfer-matrix moment is established.
No lattice-spacing-uniform physical lower bound or continuum spectral identification is established.
